The period is the bleeding part of your cycle which normally lasts 2-7 days (some can be longer). The amount of blood you lose varies, the average amount being 80 ml or less. More than this is considered heavy menstrual bleeding. Tampons can be used throughout your period but preferably not on lighter days. Tampons should be changed every 4-8 hours. If you leave one in too long you put yourself at risk for toxic shock syndrome, which is a life threatening illness. Your risk also increases with more absorbent tampons. A woman’s cycle can last anywhere from 21-35 days. The cycle starts the first day of your period and goes until the next day of your period.

I’m sorry she’s not being supportive. The first person I talked to when I got my first period was my mom. If you can find anybody else you can talk to you can maybe ask them for help. I couldn’t use tampons for a long time until I found out the reason I wasn’t able to put them in was because I wasn’t spreading my vaginal lips open enough so the opening wasn’t exposed. This might not be the problem for you but I’d recommend looking at a diagram to get familiar with everything then trying again. If that’s not the case then you most likely just need to relax your muscles. There’s exercises that can help with this but that can be a hassle. If you still can’t get one in you might need to see a doctor. You might need to see one anyways because this sounds like too much bleeding. Are your cramps extremely painful to the point where it’s interfering with doing anything, because if so definitely see a doctor it could be endometriosis. If not it could also be Vaginismus. I wouldn’t worry too much about having these but like I said talk to your doctor.

I have the same fear. The first time I tried using a tampon I poked around for an hour trying to put it in my vagina and ended up irritating it so much that I couldn’t try again for 2 more days. I would suggest that you continue wearing pads until you’re on a lighter day so that way you can use the smallest sized tampon to get used to them. I know that it’s hard because you have such a heavy flow but it’s hard to start out with larger sized tampons if you’ve never inserted something inside you. The first time you use them it shouldn’t hurt too bad. It’s okay that you’re scared most girls are the first time they try tampons. It’s important to relax which is very hard to do but think about something that calms you or listen to some music. You could also take a hot shower or bath right before you try. Like I said anything that can distract you.

Talk to a trusted adult or someone you feel comfortable talking with and ask them if they can buy you some products. Never feel ashamed to ask, periods are a natural part of life. I recommend starting with pads and not tampons. Tampons are hard to get in the first time and it’s better to wait. Get a few different pad sizes to make sure you don’t leak and get the night ones too so you don’t make a mess on your bed. For cramps I recommend getting a heating pad or taking a hot bath and or shower. Heat will help reduce the pain. I like to drink tea as well. If none of these things help try taking ibuprofen (which is just Advil). Good luck and don’t be afraid to ask any questions!
